title: Frontiers: Determining the Validity of Large Language Models for Automated Perceptual Analysis
authors: Peiyao Li; Noah Castelo; Zsolt Katona; Miklós Sárváry
eligible_reason: Not a DiD design. The paper compares LLM (GPT-Neo, GPT-4) and human perceptual similarity judgments of car brands (triplet agreement rates, perceptual maps). The only panel-style regression (triplet_method_calculations.R line 879) is plm(agree ~ treatment, index='year', model='within') on 160 GPT-4 runs, where treatment = 1 if the prompt specifies the trade-in year; it is a prompt-variation comparison with year FE, not a unit-level adoption design.
design_notes: R (plm, lm) plus Python EvoMap notebook. Regressions: lm of perceived attributes on respondent income/gender/age (heterogeneity), and the prompt-year 'treatment' regression on JD Power trade-in agreement rates. No units, no adoption dates, no event time.

specs.exclusion_reason: not a DiD: prompt-condition indicator (year specified vs not) across GPT-4 runs with year FE; no units adopting a treatment over time
specs.reported_location: car trade-in validation (location unknown; no article text)

specs.exclusion_reason: cross-sectional OLS of perceived attributes on respondent demographics

data_files_note: Survey and LLM output CSVs shipped. readme.txt: JD Power trade-in tables have noise added for confidentiality.
data_provenance_note: LLM outputs and survey data appear original; the JD Power trade-in tables are disguised (noise added). Moot: no DiD design.
software_notes: R (plm, lmtest, ggplot2) and Python (evomap notebook)
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF). Prescore 2 came from the plm within regression on a prompt-condition indicator; no staggered adoption design.
